environment: Local PostgreSQL integration database; synthetic fixtures; default Node heap and PostgreSQL settings

baselineBeforeBulkAndPagedComponents.projectionAssumption: same cohort mix and query latency; extrapolation, not a production runtime measurement

interpretation: Durations time reconciliation itself and exclude synthetic fixture creation and rollback.
Each projection assumes the same fixture mix and local query latency; none is a measured production execution time.
The mixed fixture deliberately contains 500 duplicate groups among 2000 rows; production component ownership and conflict counts must be measured by its dry run.
Node stores four graph-parent bytes per source row, numeric edge pages of 5000 rows, and one component plus its metadata page; largest component size is reported.
History payloads and full before snapshots stay in PostgreSQL; database work_mem governs spillable sorts. No Node heap override, forced GC, or timeout escalation was used.
Heap deltas are observations across an operation, not peak retained memory bounds; negative deltas reflect garbage collection.

Fresh identities use set-based creation only when aliases are disjoint and unowned, stable/property evidence agrees, and there is at most one canonical row; conflicts and canonical duplicates remain on the audited resolver.
The 25 PostgreSQL cases prove reference/history/audit preservation, repeated execution, rollback, alias ownership boundaries, whitespace normalization, and one added source advisory lock.
